newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian second-tier shares send market to record.
newsitem.headline: Russian second-tier shares send market to record.

text.p: The Russian Trading System (RTS) index of leading shares surged to a record on Tuesday but traders said less well known shares showed the highest gains.
The RTS 24-share index rose 2.96 percent to 329.83 on a total market volume of $46 million.

Regional utility Lenenergo jumped to $0.950 at close from $0.720 at Monday's close. Moscow City Telephone (MGTS) preferred shares rose to $0.90 from $0.80, and oil company Sakhalinmorneftegaz rose to $2.50 from $2.25.
National utility UES rose to $0.2339 from $0.2170 on over 38 million share turnover. Oil company Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.759 from $0.710 on over 5.5 million share volume.
Alfa Capital trader Dmitry Lobanov said demand for non-liquid shares was higher than on Monday, especially among telecoms.
Svyazinform-Irkutsk rose to $1.45 from $1.15 and Chelyabsvyazinform prefs rose to $30.00 from $28.50.
"There could be a correction on the RTS-2 (less liquid shares trading system) on some of the most traded shares, but generally slow growth will continue," Lobanov said.
